result: In 43 CFS (21 severe, 22 less severe) vs 29 controls, chronotropic baroreflex sensitivity fell more on active standing in CFS, significantly only in severe CFS, while systolic BP was maintained; BRS reduction during a speech task was normal in all groups.
reason: Cardiovagal baroreflex measure matches the finding's vagal/baroreflex detail (Walitt 2024); adds a standing and severity-subgroup result.

result: After 20 min cycling at 70% predicted max, C4a (not C3a or C5a) rose at 6 h only in CFS (32 vs 29 controls).
reason: already cited: this is the Sorensen 2003 C4a exercise study named in the finding detail.

result: In 21 CFS vs 20 controls, salivary and plasma cortisol responses to the Trier Social Stress Test did not differ, but in vitro dexamethasone suppressed LPS-stimulated IL-6 (p=0.004) and TNF-alpha (p=0.01) more in CFS, indicating enhanced glucocorticoid sensitivity.
reason: Not an in vivo ACTH/dexamethasone challenge, so not a replication; it adds a peripheral immune-cell measure of enhanced glucocorticoid sensitivity.

result: Systematic review: low NK-cell findings were inversely associated with study quality, T-cell and cytokine abnormalities were not, and no consistent pattern of immune abnormality was found.
reason: Supports the method-artefact explanation for the low NK signal; note it concerns NK levels more than cytotoxicity.

result: In 12 CFS vs 11 sedentary matched controls on ramp exercise, peak VO2 was lower and perceived exertion higher in CFS; free Trp/BCAA and free Trp/LNAA ratios were higher and tyrosine lower.
reason: Same measure (peak VO2 on a single maximal test), same direction; small sample.

result: By radioligand assay, anti-muscarinic M1 (CHRM1) antibodies were raised in CFS (n=60, p<0.0001 vs 30 controls; 53.3% positive) and linked to muscle-weakness scores (1.81 vs 1.18, p<0.01); anti-mu-opioid, 5-HT1A and D2 antibodies were in 15.2%, 1.7% and 5.0%.
reason: The M1 receptor and other neurotransmitter receptors, measured by radioligand assay, fit the neural-autoantibody finding better than the beta2/M3/M4 ELISA claim.

result: Impedance cardiography in 38 CFS (18 severe) vs 27 sedentary controls showed lower stroke volume and cardiac output in severe CFS than in controls and less ill patients.
reason: Same variable (stroke volume), same direction, with the severity pattern of Hurwitz 2009.

result: Population-based Wichita survey (7,162 adults screened, clinical exam): CFS point prevalence 235/100,000 (95% CI 142-327), 373 in women vs 83 in men; 1-year incidence 180/100,000.
reason: Independent population estimate in the 0.2-1% range with a female excess of about 4.5x.

result: In 19 CFS vs 11 sedentary controls, post-ischaemic peak blood flow, PCr recovery after submaximal exercise (31P-MRS) and NIRS oxygen resaturation did not differ.
reason: Another null 31P-MRS study, matching the finding's 'no consistent group abnormality' arm; it measures PCr recovery, not pH.

result: In 22 monozygotic twin pairs discordant for CFS, CFS twins reported much worse sleep, but polysomnography showed little objective difference apart from a higher percentage of REM sleep, suggesting sleep-state misperception.
reason: The co-twin PSG found no meaningful latency, wake or efficiency deficit, against the finding's objective-difference claim; the label 'replicates' was wrong.
